$description: Design tokens for the Xforge design system, in the W3C Design Tokens Format Module shape (2025.10). THE authority for every design value the product renders. Three tiers: primitives are raw values, semantics name a ROLE, and nothing reaches past a role to a primitive -- the generator refuses that edge. COLOUR ROLES ARE FLAT AND EXPLICITLY PAIRED, which is the one structural departure worth naming: a role and its foreground carry the same stem, so `card` / `card-foreground` states its own contrast pair instead of leaving it to be inferred from a family. That is shadcn's convention, and it is adopted because it makes the contrast policy read directly off the names AND because a component or block written against shadcn works here unmodified. Two axes compose and neither owns the other's territory: theme owns colour, density owns geometry. generated/ is DERIVED and never hand-edited (law 27).

color.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Raw values with no role. Nothing outside the semantic tier may reference these -- a primitive carries a value and no meaning, so a mode has nothing to rebind.

50.$description: The page. Deepened from #f7f9fb, where it was 1.8 CIEDE2000 from a white card and the surface separation the elevation policy claims was below the threshold at which anyone can see it.

100.$description: The recessed well and the muted surface. Deepened with neutral.50 so the two stay 3.7 apart.

ink.$description: The dark theme's own ramp. Not an inversion of neutral: a dark surface needs its own steps, and reusing the light ramp upside down produces the flat, muddy dark mode this ramp exists to avoid.

teal.$description: The interactive accent. Teal rather than blue or green: it reads as a thing you can press without being the green half of the red/green pair colour deficiency collapses.

300.$description: THE DARK STATUTORY FOREGROUND, and a taupe rather than a brass on purpose. At #cbb47e it sat 3.7 CIEDE2000 from amber.300, so statutory and warning read as one colour on a dark ground. 13.7 now.

brass.$description: STATUTORY. Malaysian payroll is saturated with facts that are neither actions, errors nor warnings -- EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB rates and ceilings are law. Painted as `info` they read as advice; painted as body text they disappear. Brass reads as fixed by regulation without competing with the accent.

shadow.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. The ink a shadow is drawn in. Two steps because a shadow reads as one object only when a tight key layer sits over a wide ambient one; a single blur reads as a grey rectangle.

key-dark.$description: Black at 45%. On a near-black page a shadow is weak; on a raised surface it is not.

none.$description: Fully transparent, and it exists as a NAMED value rather than as the string "transparent" so the dark theme rebinds a role to a token rather than to a literal.

space.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. A 4px scale, so spacing is chosen from a set rather than invented per screen.

size.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Lengths that are not spacing: radii, strokes, type sizes and control floors.

font.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. IBM Plex: drawn for technical and business contexts, with true tabular figures. The system stack trails each as a fallback so the product is legible before the webfont arrives.

sans.$value: IBM Plex Sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

mono.$value: IBM Plex Mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace

weight.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Named for the weight rather than the role, so `font-medium` means what it says in any component.

leading.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. RATIOS CHOSEN SO EACH SIZE LANDS ON THE 4px GRID the space scale already uses (4/8/12/16/24/32). 12x1.3333=16, 14x1.4286=20, 16x1.5=24, 22x1.2727=28, 24x1.3333=32, 32x1.25=40. Unitless rather than px on purpose: a ratio scales with the user's text size, so the grid holds under enlargement, where a px line-height would break exactly there. Named by magnitude, not by role -- a primitive named for a meaning has taken the semantic layer's job.

tracking.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Letterspacing, and there are two values because there are two call sites. Two components were letterspacing keyboard shortcuts with Tailwind's `tracking-widest` -- a value this file had never heard of, reachable because `--tracking-*` was the one namespace left open.

easing.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Carbon productive curves. ASYMMETRIC on purpose: an element should speed up quickly and slow down smoothly. Entrance decelerates into place, exit accelerates away, standard does both.

component.$description: COMPONENT tier: geometry a component needs and no semantic role names (ADR-031 Decision 6). Each token aliases a SEMANTIC role, never a number, so density rebinds it. The tier was empty until the Switch (ADR-034 step 8): upstream sized its track in hand-typed pixels, and a switch track is exactly what this tier is for. The thumb travels by flex alignment, so no distance is minted.

semantic.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Every role a component may reach for. A component names a role; a role names a value. Colour roles are flat and paired by stem -- `card` and `card-foreground` -- so each contrast pair is stated by the names themselves. DESTRUCTIVE IS AN ACTION, NOT A STATUS. It is a strong fill with a light foreground, like `primary`, because it paints a button somebody presses. `warning`, `success`, `info` and `statutory` are status BACKDROPS -- pale surfaces carrying dark text -- because they paint a region somebody reads. Both conventions are shadcn's; the distinction is which question the role answers.

space.$description: Geometry roles. Density rebinds these; theme never touches them.

size.$description: Lengths with no Tailwind namespace of their own -- a stroke, a focus ring. Components reach these through `@utility` blocks that read the custom property, because Tailwind has no border-width or outline-width theme namespace.

control.$description: Named `control.min-size` because the accessibility policy asserts that exact path against the WCAG 2.5.8 floor in every mode.

target.$description: The WCAG 2.5.8 floor. Named `target.minimum` because the accessibility policy asserts that exact path in every mode -- density may not shrink it.

radius.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Structured at rest, soft where interactive. 0 structures, 4 refines, 8 interacts, 12 contains, 16 overlays. `square` and `full` are Tailwind statics rather than tokens -- `rounded-full` is calc(infinity * 1px), not a theme key -- and are recorded here rather than minted.

control.$description: THE SIGNATURE. Buttons, inputs, selects — 8px against a 40px control.

type.$description: Font sizes, named by ROLE. The typography policy asserts these three paths and proves hierarchy survives every density -- a scale named sm/base/lg would state no hierarchy for it to check.

ease.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Which curve a change uses, named for what it does.

elevation.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Five planes, and the default is flat. A card groups; a shadow floats. Ordinary content stays on the page and is separated by surface, border and space -- elevation is the LAST containment tool, used only where a surface genuinely sits above another. If everything floats, nothing has elevation.

flat.$description: The page and everything permanent on it: card, table, form, rail, tabs.

raised.$description: A sticky surface once content has scrolled beneath it -- the one case with real spatial meaning. NOT hover, and not a clickable card.

floating.$description: A menu, a popover, a tooltip: it has left the page and will return.

overlay.$description: A sheet, a drawer, a command palette: it sits over the workspace.

modal.$description: A dialog. The SCRIM does most of the perceptual work here; this is the shadow that keeps the surface from looking pasted onto it.

layer.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Stacking order, which is NOT elevation -- one is rendering order, the other is visual depth. Two values because two are in use. An eight-step ladder for a product with one dialog is infrastructure ahead of a measured pain; the third value arrives with the first component that genuinely needs to sit above a portalled surface.

local.$description: Within one component: an avatar badge, a scroll button.

overlay.$description: A portalled surface above the application.

icon.$description: SEMANTIC layer. An icon that does not move with density is the same defect as a control that does not: 42 icons were sized from Tailwind numbers and stayed 16px whichever mode the product was in.

motion.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Named for the kind of change, not the number of milliseconds. `press` must feel immediate; `overlay` carries visual weight.

none.$description: motion neutralised — what every duration becomes under prefers-reduced-motion

content.$description: SEMANTIC layer. How wide a thing is allowed to get. A workspace is fluid and has no entry here; everything that is READ has a ceiling.

shell.$description: SEMANTIC layer. The persistent frame, which is a different system from the workspace inside it. These were hardcoded -- `w-60` on the rail is 240px, which is the number this names.

$modes.$description: Two axes that compose. Theme owns colour, density owns geometry, and a token rebound by both is refused -- their selectors have equal specificity, so the winner would be decided by emission order rather than by design.

density.$description: Compact is what makes this usable for a bureau processing many companies. It never rebinds `semantic.size.target`: the WCAG 2.5.8 floor holds in every mode, and the generator asserts it.

duration.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. The productive band only. Motion in a working tool is feedback, not choreography -- it confirms that something happened and gets out of the way.

none.$description: NOT ZERO, and the distinction is why this is a token. A zero-duration transition does not fire `transitionend`, so a component waiting for that event would hang for exactly the people who asked for less motion. 0.01ms is imperceptible and still fires.

breakpoint.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Material 3 window size classes, which describe the AVAILABLE WINDOW rather than a device. Tailwind ships 640/768/1024/1280/1536 and not one of them coincides with these -- so every `md:` in this system was firing at a number nobody chose.
